look: Cinematic office film with hands on laptops, close up screens and coworkers chatting on a sofa.
magic: It shows the bot doing real chores inside tools people already use, filmed like a calm real workday.

look: School kids skit with a 'days since last accident' sign, show and tell, and note screens on top.
magic: Kids saying adult work lines is a cheap, safe joke that everyone shares.

look: Dark security diagram, prompt box, CRM screens with a founder bubble, founder talking in a loft, subtitles.
magic: Naming a giant partner (AWS) in the first line borrows trust before the demo starts.

look: Vertical white terminal typing one install command, then 'Agent Skills now available' and two logos side by side.
magic: One copy-paste command plus a video made by that command is instant proof and a free how-to.

look: Dark aurora gradients, huge single words (Create, Iterate, Prototype) and a glowing prompt and voice bar.
magic: Five upgrades told as one word each make a big update easy to remember and easy to screenshot.

look: Black screen, a white circle face reacts, coloured faces crowd in, '1 day. 20+ launches'.
magic: Cute characters and a countdown number create hype with zero product details.

look: Cinematic short film: a chef, a businesswoman and a suit each hand their chores to an AI browser.
magic: Normal people in real jobs make the tool feel useful to everyone, not only tech fans.

look: Soft white type, investor logos, founders in hazy light, product screens and a keynote stage shot.
magic: A huge number told quietly, with the product and a vision, makes the raise feel like a story and not a brag.

look: Plain white screen recording of the app on a soft drop shadow, with a cursor doing the work.
magic: It shows one input (your website) turning into a full team of agents, so the promise is proven in under a minute.

look: Calm green dune Mac desktop, a floating command bar runs tasks across apps, then a phone view and logo.
magic: It looks like your own Mac, so the viewer instantly pictures the feature on their own computer.

look: Cinematic date skit where a guy uses a hidden AI overlay to lie on a date, with glowing UI panels.
magic: Controversy plus a relatable social moment made people argue, and arguing spreads it.

look: Presenter in a lived in home talks to and points at a robot, product close ups, a tweet wall.
magic: Talking and pointing at a robot is a natural human gesture, so the demo feels obvious.

look: Warm close ups of the bookmark device in books on a desk, the founder talking by a pool, the phone app.
magic: Warm tactile shots make a small gadget feel like a gift you want.

look: Big serif type, then a montage of real users' clips with tweet bubbles, ending on a clean title card.
magic: Real people's results do the bragging, so the launch feels earned and not like an ad.

look: Real people asking 'How do I use Claude' in search bubbles over green, then a calm title card.
magic: It starts from the exact questions beginners type, so everyone feels it is for them.

look: Clean white Apple style grid of apps on iPhone, iPad and Vision Pro with simple labels and a big closing line.
magic: Many fast wins in a row make 'it can do almost anything' feel true.

look: Warm living room, a man on a sofa talks to camera, then close ups of his phone running coding agents.
magic: It shows coding away from the desk, which feels like a small freedom everyone wants.

look: Founder on black, cut to real customers at work with name and result titles, then back to the founder.
magic: The founder sets the belief, and real customers with names prove it.

look: Pastel slides with one short line each, a brain wave graphic and the logo; the product is never shown.
magic: Hiding the product while saying something bold (control things with your mind) builds pure curiosity.

look: Dark dot matrix terminal, a HUD face scan, giant '$250M VALUATION' type, seedlings and a man in a field.
magic: The twist that the AI ran its own fundraise makes the raise itself the product demo.

look: Dark documentary style: founder backstory text, a crowded room of laptops, '$15 Million' and a punchy last line.
magic: It turns a raise into a rebel origin story with a slogan people can quote.

look: Cinematic desert film with friends and lanterns, poetic subtitles, the wearable barely shown.
magic: It sells a feeling (being present) and hides the product, which makes people curious.

look: Glitchy warning labels (fear, rage bait) on black, then a soft pastel feed and a calm cream logo card.
magic: It names a shared enemy in one glance, then the product is the relief.

look: Movie trailer parody: a goddess on cliffs and waves, epic shots, an app notification, 'In theaters now'.
magic: Treating a travel app like a blockbuster is funny and makes people watch to see the joke land.

look: Flat illustration intro, a cartoon guide, real app screens with a green mascot and a small founder face bubble.
magic: It opens with a bold opinion (AI is making kids dumber) that people want to argue with, then shows the fix.

look: Founder talking head lit by a warm lamp, bold kinetic subtitles, a Slack thread where the agent replies.
magic: It opens on a pain every engineer feels (team about to snap), then shows the fix inside a tool they live in.

look: Founder in a bright office talks to camera, then colourful design canvas and agent cards, ending on a free offer.
magic: Raised money plus a free giveaway gives people a reason to repost and comment right now.

look: 'Human vs Wispr Flow' challenge on a white set, real people try to beat it for a Porsche, accuracy chart.
magic: A big prize and a simple challenge make people watch to the end to see who wins.

look: Clear retainer on black, a man controls his phone with his tongue, macro product shots, 10 seconds.
magic: It is so strange you must rewatch it, and it is only 10 seconds long.

look: Founder in a clean studio, ring macro shots, a 'premium titanium frame' card and app logos flying in.
magic: It connects a tiny device to the AI tools you already use, so it feels useful on day one.

look: Prompt box to finished website, cut with a founder talking head, a news headline and a rising revenue chart.
magic: It sells the end result (money) and not the tool, then uses a scary headline to make waiting feel risky.

look: White serif text cards plus a MacBook with a small top bar that listens, then docs and slides appear.
magic: Short serif lines name the pain, then one voice command finishes a whole task, which is easy to believe.

look: Drone footage of a reactor build site under one fixed overlay of the raise amount and investor logos.
magic: The overlay never moves, so the number sinks in while real work behind it proves it is real.

look: Heist film style team intro: each person gets a huge yellow name card and an absurd skill.
magic: It makes the team the content, so people follow the people, not only the product.

look: Two people chat at a table with a MacBook in a library, then a screen demo with picture in picture.
magic: Two builders talking like friends make a technical bridge between two tools feel simple.

look: Lo-fi typed captions, a repeated 'so let's see what it can do' text wall, then real Claude chat driving a timeline.
magic: It feels made by a builder, not an agency, and shows Claude using the app with no cut tricks.

look: Founder sits outside on a bench with a laptop, explains with his hands, big subtitles, quick screen cuts.
magic: A real founder explaining one clear upgrade in plain words feels honest and easy to share.

look: One founder talking head in a warm library with glass pill lower thirds for the numbers and investors.
magic: One person, one number, plain thanks: simple and human, and the number does the work.

look: A developer talks at his desk, a big title card, then a dark editor showing the plugin file.
magic: A real engineer showing the actual file makes a standard feel safe and ready to use today.

look: Archival construction film into cinematic site footage, a founder in hi-vis, a control room and a burning logo.
magic: A clear villain (America forgot how to build) and a founder on site make a mission people want to join.

look: Webcam style customer clips with name tags and dollar wins, then two founders on a sofa.
magic: Customers saying the numbers is more believable than the founders saying them.

look: Fake film set opener that breaks the fourth wall, then cream cards, phone screens and hand drawn icons.
magic: The fake-out first five seconds buys attention, and the honest 'that wasn't real' earns trust for the demo.

look: Archival film clips with timecodes, a founder at a cosy desk explaining, and a search screen.
magic: A big idea told with history first makes a new category feel inevitable.

look: Vertical handheld style: click the Codex icon, shaky close ups of screen text, a 'ChatCut x Codex' card.
magic: It rides a big platform name (Codex) and says 'free if you already pay', which removes the last reason not to try.

look: Serif model names, a founder talking outdoors on a deck, real app screen recordings, an ask at the end.
magic: 'I quit OpenAI to build this' is a personal stake that makes people stop and listen.

look: Founder talking head with floating phone cards, a cartoon mascot face, bold purple and yellow panels and subtitles.
magic: A friendly mascot and a clear before and after make an abstract AI service feel like a real teammate.

look: Archival mission control film, a typed 'What's the limit?' line, the earth's horizon and a quiet logo.
magic: Old space footage ties a small startup to a huge human story, so it feels important.

look: A developer on a sofa explains, cut to real websites using the new feature.
magic: Real use cases show why a small API feature matters.

look: Stark white page, huge black capital text, a simple harness to gateway diagram and benchmark charts.
magic: Bold text plus one diagram explains where the tool sits in your stack in seconds, no voiceover needed.

look: Dark terminal cards with big caps names of real tools (ESPN, Domino's), then a 3 step 'how does it work'.
magic: Famous everyday brands make a developer tool feel fun and concrete.

look: A famous TV actor in a bath and robe runs his whole day by talking to a small device, glass UI cards.
magic: A known character in a silly setting gets the click, and the product is the punchline.

look: Black space with light streaks colliding, the logo, 'AGI is coming' and a handle typed into a URL bar.
magic: Scarcity (grab your handle before someone else) turns a tease into an action.

look: Keynote style stage with giant glasses, face close ups wearing them, a HUD over a lab and a city.
magic: Promising coding agents 'anywhere' sparks the imagination of every developer.

look: Soft text cards, 'With Claude on Shipper', paste a URL, a phone mockup app builds itself.
magic: One tiny input (a URL) and one big output (an app) is the clearest possible demo.

look: Acted skit in a bookshelf office: a nervous guy pitches, a stern investor reads papers, a deadpan end card.
magic: Awkward deadpan acting makes a dry money announcement funny and rewatchable.

look: Founder face bubble over a phone screen, step labels Dictate, Edit, Translate, green subtitles.
magic: Three named steps with the founder's face make it a mini lesson, not an ad.

look: Raw split screen: an agent terminal on the left and a browser doing the task on the right, no edits.
magic: No edits means no tricks, and developers trust raw footage most.

look: Black terminal, a file diff list, browser views with red bug tags, then red X marks flip to green checks.
magic: Red to green is the most satisfying ending in software, and it names Claude Code and Codex up front.

look: CGI rockets and orbit stations, a huge caps slogan and a legal disclaimer card.
magic: Big scale visuals sell an ambition before there is anything to show.

look: Raw vertical iPhone screen recording where a command sends a push notification instantly.
magic: Short, instant and personal: the payoff happens in seconds on a real device.

look: White prompt bar types a request, cuts to cinematic generated shots, a model list card and the URL.
magic: Showing results inside the apps people already use makes the integration feel like a free upgrade.

look: Claude Code terminal running one slash command, a health score climbing from 22 to 100 with confetti.
magic: A score going up is a game, and the exact command is shown so anyone can copy it.

look: Moody black and white desk scenes, a man pushes to talk on phone and Mac, text appears in a terminal.
magic: Slow, premium, almost silent footage makes push-to-talk feel like a luxury tool and not a utility.

look: Terminal over a landscape wallpaper, typed lines like 'this is a real browser', fast command palette.
magic: Typed captions inside the tool itself make the demo feel playful and native.

look: Black background with one chrome card per step: Identity, Model, Skills, MCPs, Review, Create.
magic: One bold card per step turns a setup flow into something you can follow and remember.

look: White and orange, CLI commands, a results grid, an agent cursor working in Drive.
magic: Each command gets its own tiny result, so the viewer learns the tool in one watch.

look: Black background, a smiling circle face with a heart, then a simple day schedule list.
magic: A friendly face on a plain schedule makes a dry agenda feel like an event.

look: Text only kinetic type with ASCII and pixel transitions in black and white, cut to music.
magic: Made with no footage at all, so it is cheap, fast and still feels premium.
